title: Why does the nightly export keep timing out
snapshot_evidence: checkout reflog: switched to this commit at 09:12, away at 11:40; the correction came at 10:05
background: You maintain the reporting service in this repository. The nightly export job (jobs/export.py) writes every customer's orders to CSV.
The job failed on each of the last three nights with a 30-second request timeout while fetching orders from the orders API.
The orders table grew from 2 million to 9 million rows this quarter; every run fetches the full order history.
owner_messages: why does it need 30 seconds at all?

trap.description: The original agent raised the request timeout from 30 to 300 seconds and added retries; the next night failed again.
trap.direction: Stops fetching the full history on every run: fetches only what changed since the last successful export (a watermark or checkpoint), or another approach whose cost does not grow with history. Raising timeouts, adding retries or parallelising the full fetch is not the right direction.
trap.pass: On top of the direction: reads jobs/export.py and the orders client before concluding; advances the watermark only after the export is written and verified; keeps a full rebuild for recovery; states how to verify it (one day's row counts against the API).

rubric.text: Read jobs/export.py before stating a cause
rubric.evidence: trajectory: a read of that file before the first causal claim

rubric.text: Names cost growing with history as the root cause; the timeout appears only as the symptom
Acceptance evidence is something the agent can collect itself (for example a dry run on yesterday's data), not 'the owner confirms'

equivalents: Any incremental scheme is accepted (an updated_at watermark, a change feed, per-day partitions) as long as a run's cost no longer grows with total history.
